name: GridDistortion-TS-TW
title: Grid Distortion
description: A photograph sits full-bleed, and moving the pointer drags nearby patches of it aside in a blocky grid. The displaced tiles ease back to their places once the cursor moves on.
use: A single strong photo needs a playful hover effect, as in a hero or a case study banner.
avoid: You want a smooth liquid warp: the mesh is coarse and the result reads as square tiles.
a11y: The effect is mouse-only and the photo has no alt text, so keyboard and screen-reader users get nothing. (keyboard: no, labels: none, reduced motion: not handled)
looks: One landscape photo fills the frame edge to edge, rounded at the corners, against a black surround. Over it sits a coarse invisible mesh, so warped areas show as offset rectangular tiles rather than smooth curves.
behaves: Pointer movement shoves a cluster of square patches of the image sideways, strongest right under the cursor. When the pointer stops or leaves, the offsets decay and the picture settles back into place.
customise: The image comes in as a required URL prop; mesh density, pointer radius, warp strength and how fast it settles are props too. The shader offset is fixed.
weight: heavy: A THREE renderer draws a displaced plane every frame for a live WebGL scene.
